n: Fund-recovery scams and official-impersonation follow-on scams
ds: People who have already lost money to scams are targeted again by fake law firms, 'investigators' or officials who promise to recover funds, or by callers posing as police or government who direct them to pay in digital assets, gift cards, precious metals handed to couriers, or international wires.

src.t: FinCEN (US Treasury), FinCEN Alert on Money Laundering Activity Associated with Digital Asset Investment Scam Centers (FIN-2026-Alert005) (2026-09-03)

cn.rt: Repeat-victim customers moving savings after calls; branch and phone staff can intervene.

rat: Previously scammed retail customers paying from everyday, savings or retirement funds after phone contact.

ind.n: Payment to a fund-recovery service that cannot show it is legitimate
ind.cx: A prior scam victim pays a 'recovery' firm or 'lawyer' that cannot show it is genuine.
ind.fp: Engagement of a genuine, licensed law firm with verifiable credentials and standard fee arrangements.
ind.ds: A customer who has already lost money pays a firm, 'lawyer' or 'investigator' promising to recover the losses, without credible documentation, licensing or engagement terms.

ind.n: Customer says an official told them to pay in crypto, gold, gift cards or by international wire
ind.cx: The customer says police or a government agency told them to pay in crypto, gift cards, gold or by overseas wire.
ind.fp: Genuine tax or fine payments made through official, verifiable channels.
ind.ds: The customer explains a payment as instructed by someone claiming to be police, a regulator or another government body, using digital assets, precious metals, gift cards or an overseas wire.

ind.n: Savings or retirement funds withdrawn to buy gold that is handed to a courier
ind.cx: Retirement or investment savings are cashed in to buy gold that a courier will collect.
ind.fp: Genuine bullion investment held in the customer's own custody or a recognised vault.
ind.ds: The customer liquidates investment or retirement savings to buy bullion or gold and says they have been told to hand it to a courier or collector.

ind.n: Multiple prior scam alerts or repeat victimisation
ind.cx: The customer has reported a scam before and is again sending money to new payees.
ind.fp: Customers who have since become aware and are genuinely transacting.
ind.ds: Victim-side: the customer previously reported or was warned of fraud and is again sending payments to new payees.

ind.n: Customer accompanied, directed or coached by a third party
ind.cx: The customer is on the phone with, or being coached by, the 'recovery agent' or 'official' while transacting.
ind.fp: Carers, relatives or interpreters may legitimately assist; assess the customer's autonomy.
ind.ds: Another person speaks for, accompanies or dictates instructions to the customer, who may appear fearful, scripted or unable to explain the activity.

ctl.n: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
ctl.ds: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

Allows customers to nominate a trusted contact and applies tailored handling and permitted escalation when vulnerability is flagged. It adds a safeguard for customers more exposed to manipulation or coercion.

ctl.n: Cooling-off and delayed release for new payees
ctl.ds: Holds or delays the first large payment to a new payee or to changed details so the customer or institution can verify before funds leave. It buys time to detect coercion or fraud.
